packages.title: DfT LGV/HGV classification-policy QA
facts: DfT notes a policy-related classification treatment for certain alternatively fuelled vehicles up to 4.25 tonnes.
Although they can fall in an HGV weight category, the statistics place these vehicles in the LGV category for policy alignment.
Body-type classification therefore has a stated statistical convention.
Comparisons must preserve the release's classification rule.
Vehicle class labels alone cannot determine emissions.

packages.title: HEE provisional and revision-status QA
facts: The June 2026 Household Energy Efficiency release covers ECO and Green Deal measures.
The release states that the statistics are provisional.
The statistics are subject to future revisions.
The collection distinguishes headline monthly or quarterly updates from detailed annual reporting.
Provisional installation statistics must not be treated as final parcel-level energy savings.

packages.title: HEE June 2026 correction QA
facts: DESNZ corrected Table T1.6 on 25 June 2026 after identifying an error in the original publication.
The correction occurred on the publication date.
Downstream QA should retain the corrected release rather than silently using the earlier table.
A corrected table may change derived summaries.
Correction provenance must be stored with any reused value.

packages.title: HEE installation versus estimated-savings QA
facts: HEE statistics include counts of measures installed under ECO.
They also include estimated carbon and energy savings from installed measures.
An installed measure count is not the same variable as estimated carbon savings.
Estimated savings are not direct measured household emissions.
Neither measure count nor estimated savings automatically binds to a cadastral parcel.

packages.title: HEE geographical breakdown versus parcel QA
facts: HEE releases include geographical breakdowns of ECO measures.
Geographical reporting can be more detailed than national totals.
Geographical aggregation does not by itself identify a cadastral parcel.
Installation addresses and cadastral parcel geometry require a separate identity-matching process.
No parcel emissions value should be inferred solely from area-level delivery statistics.

packages.title: New-dwellings statistics-in-development QA
facts: MHCLG labels the new-dwelling energy-efficiency series as Official Statistics in Development.
The January-to-March 2026 release is based on England new dwellings.
The statistics may be refined in response to user feedback.
The development status should remain visible in downstream use.
Statistics-in-development status does not imply poor quality but does require version caution.

packages.title: New-dwelling EPC source QA
facts: The new-dwelling energy-efficiency statistics use EPCs lodged on the Energy Performance of Buildings Register.
The series reports property type, heating systems and key energy-efficiency characteristics.
Reported features include heat pumps and solar PV.
An EPC record is a building-performance record rather than measured annual GHG emissions.
EPC-derived characteristics require separate parcel identity and activity data before parcel emissions estimation.

packages.title: New-dwelling Part L standard QA
facts: The series monitors Part L energy-efficiency standards for new dwellings in England.
Part L sets energy-performance standards for new dwellings and non-domestic buildings.
The statistical series estimates how new dwellings relate to the Part L 2021 Standard.
Compliance or design characteristics are not equivalent to observed annual energy consumption.
Part L status alone cannot establish parcel-level GHG emissions.

packages.title: UK ETS maritime start-date QA
facts: Domestic maritime emissions entered the UK ETS from 1 July 2026.
Offshore vessels are scheduled for inclusion from 1 January 2027.
The first maritime scheme year therefore covers only part of calendar year 2026.
Scheme-year dates must be preserved when comparing maritime emissions.
UK ETS maritime scope is a regulatory boundary rather than a parcel boundary.

packages.title: UK ETS maritime first-surrender timing QA
facts: Maritime operators must submit verified annual emissions reports for a scheme year by 31 March of the following year.
For the first two maritime scheme years, the Authority permits double-surrender timing.
Allowances for 2026 and 2027 maritime emissions are due by 30 April 2028.
Surrender timing is not the same as the emissions reference period.
Allowance surrender dates must not be used as emission dates.

packages.title: UK ETS installation thermal-input threshold QA
facts: UK ETS regulated installation activities include fuel combustion where total rated thermal input exceeds 20 MW.
The rule has stated exclusions, including installations whose primary purpose is hazardous or municipal waste incineration.
Thermal-input threshold is a regulatory eligibility criterion.
A threshold does not state the installation's actual annual GHG emissions.
An installation threshold cannot be applied to arbitrary parcels without confirming regulated activity and boundary.

packages.title: Northern Ireland electricity ETS boundary QA
facts: Participating guidance states that Northern Ireland electricity generators remain in the EU ETS.
This treatment follows the Ireland/Northern Ireland Protocol.
UK ETS and EU ETS regulatory coverage must therefore be kept distinct.
Scheme membership cannot be inferred solely from UK geography.
Parcel or facility emissions require the correct scheme and operator boundary.

packages.title: UK ETS HSE threshold QA
facts: For the 2026-2030 allocation period a non-hospital small emitter must emit less than 25,000 tonnes CO2e per scheme year.
Where applicable it must also have total rated thermal input below 35 MW.
These thresholds determine HSE eligibility conditions, not parcel emissions.
HSE status uses installation-level regulatory boundaries.
Thresholds must not be used as estimated emissions values.

packages.title: UK ETS HSE target versus allowance QA
facts: Hospitals and small emitters use annual emissions targets under simplified provisions.
HSE targets are distinct from free allowance allocations.
The UK ETS reports collection publishes HSE emissions and targets separately from allocation tables.
A target is not a verified emissions measurement.
Target data cannot be assigned to a parcel without installation identity and geometry.

packages.title: UK ETS registry account/allocation QA
facts: The UK ETS Registry publishes public reports on operator account holders and allocations.
Registry account-holder reports identify regulated account structures.
Free allocation data represent allowances allocated under the scheme.
Allocation amounts are not the same as verified installation emissions.
Registry account data require installation matching before any spatial attribution.

packages.title: UK ETS maritime registry-account QA
facts: The UK ETS Registry publishes maritime operator holding-account reports.
Maritime operator accounts are distinct from installation operator holding accounts.
Account existence shows registry participation rather than a measured emissions amount.
Maritime account-holder data do not identify a land parcel emission source.
Any spatial analysis must preserve the operator and vessel regulatory boundary.

packages.title: DESNZ 2025 provisional sector-share QA
facts: DESNZ provisionally estimates 2025 UK net territorial GHG emissions at 367 MtCO2e.
Domestic transport accounted for 31% of the provisional 2025 total.
Buildings and product uses accounted for 22%, while agriculture accounted for 13%.
The provisional statistics are subject to revision when final 2025 estimates are published.
Provisional national sector shares must not be presented as parcel measurements.

packages.title: DESNZ provisional methodology/projection QA
facts: Provisional 2025 energy-related emissions use provisional Energy Trends energy statistics.
Some non-energy sectors use the latest Energy and Emissions Projections in the provisional method.
The release states that agriculture, waste and LULUCF 2025 estimates are largely derived from projections.
Provisional estimates do not use the same complete methodology as final inventory estimates.
Projected national-sector emissions must not be treated as measured local or parcel values.
